items.prose: A pension pot of £9,600 is split between shares and bonds. Three eighths of the pot is in shares and the rest is in bonds.

parts.question: What percentage of the pot is in shares? Give your answer as a percentage.

widget.label: Share of the pot in shares

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide 3 by 8, then count the hundredths.

byKey.decimal: You typed the decimal 0.375 in a per cent box, which reads as 0.375%. Move the point two places: 37.5%.
byKey.upside-down: You divided 8 by 3. Three eighths is 3 out of 8, so it is $3 \div 8 = 0.375$, or 37.5%.

explain.text: $\tfrac{3}{8} = 0.375$, and 0.375 is 37.5 hundredths. So 37.5% of the pot is in shares.

parts.question: Using 37.5% from part 1, how much of the pot is in shares, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Find 1% of £9,600 first, then take 37.5 lots of it.

byKey.ten-times: That is 375% of the pot. 37.5% is 37.5 lots of 1%, and 1% of £9,600 is £96.
byKey.tenth: That is 3.75% of the pot. 1% is £96, so 37.5% is $37.5 \times 96 = 3{,}600$.
byKey.bonds: That is the bonds, the other 62.5%. The shares are 37.5% of £9,600: £3,600.

parts.question: The shares rise by 15% over the year. Using £3,600 from part 2 and one multiplier, what are the shares worth now, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Keep the whole as 1 and add 0.15, then multiply once.

byKey.multiplier-1-5: You multiplied by 1.5, which is a 50% rise. 15% is 0.15, so the multiplier is 1.15.
byKey.rise-only: That is the rise alone. Add it to the £3,600, or multiply by 1.15 in one step.
byKey.bonds: That is 15% added to the £6,000 of bonds. The shares were £3,600, so they are now £4,140.

explain.text: A 15% rise keeps the whole and adds 0.15, so the multiplier is 1.15. $3{,}600 \times 1.15 = 4{,}140$, so the shares are worth £4,140.

parts.question: Over the same year the £6,000 of bonds falls by 4%. Using one multiplier, what are the bonds worth now, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite. A fall takes 0.04 away from 1, then you multiply once.

byKey.rise: You multiplied by 1.04, which is a rise. A fall of 4% multiplies by 0.96.
byKey.fall-only: That is the fall alone. The bonds are left with $6{,}000 - 240 = 5{,}760$.
byKey.multiplier-0-6: You took 0.4 from 1. A 4% fall is 0.04, so the multiplier is 0.96.

explain.text: A 4% fall leaves 96% of the value, so the multiplier is 0.96. $6{,}000 \times 0.96 = 5{,}760$, so the bonds are worth £5,760.

parts.question: Using shares of £4,140 and bonds of £5,760, what percentage of the pot is now in shares? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

widget.label: Share of the pot in shares now

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the two new values to get the whole, then divide the shares by it.

byKey.old-total: You divided by the old £9,600. The pot is now $4{,}140 + 5{,}760 = 9{,}900$, which gives 41.8%.
byKey.unchanged: That is the share before the year. Shares rose and bonds fell, so the share has moved.
byKey.bonds-base: You divided by the bonds alone. The whole is both together: £9,900.

explain.text: The whole is now $4{,}140 + 5{,}760 = 9{,}900$. The shares are $4{,}140 \div 9{,}900 \approx 0.418$ of it, so 41.8%. The share has drifted up from 37.5% without any trade.

items.prose: A phone contract costs £30.00 a month. Each April the price rises by the inflation rate plus 3.9 percentage points. This year inflation is 3.2%.

parts.question: What is the total rise, written as a decimal?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the two percentages, then divide by 100.

byKey.one-place: You moved the point one place. 7.1% is $7.1 \div 100 = 0.071$.
byKey.no-move: That is the percentage, 7.1. As a decimal it is $7.1 \div 100 = 0.071$.

explain.text: The rise is $3.2 + 3.9 = 7.1$ per cent. Dividing by 100 gives 0.071.

parts.question: Using a rise of 0.071, what single number do you multiply the old price by? Give your answer as a decimal.

feedback.correct: Keep the whole, 1, and add the rise: $1 + 0.071 = 1.071$.
feedback.generic: Not quite. The new price is the old price plus the rise, so start from 1.

byKey.fall: You took 0.071 away from 1, which is a fall. A rise adds it: 1.071.
byKey.rise-only: Multiplying by 0.071 gives the rise alone. To get the new price add 1: 1.071.
byKey.one-place: That is $1 + 0.71$, a 71% rise. The rise is 0.071, so the multiplier is 1.071.

explain.text: The new price is the whole old price plus 0.071 of it. That is $1 + 0.071 = 1.071$ times the old price.

parts.question: Using the multiplier 1.071, what is the new monthly price, in pounds? Give your answer to the nearest penny.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Multiply the old £30.00 by 1.071.

byKey.rise-only: That is the rise alone. The new price is $30.00 + 2.13 = 32.13$.
byKey.one-place: That is $30.00 \times 1.71$, a 71% rise. With 1.071 the price is £32.13.
byKey.fall: That is $30.00 \times 0.929$, a fall. A rise multiplies by 1.071: £32.13.

byKey.saving: That is the saving, £20.13, as a share of £32.13. The SIM-only price itself is 37.3%.

items.prose: A saver holds £18,000 in an account paying 4.6% interest a year. Interest above a £500 tax-free allowance is taxed at 40%.

parts.question: How much interest does the account pay in a year, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Find 1% of £18,000, then take 4.6 lots of it.

parts.question: Using interest of £828, how much tax is paid on it, in pounds? Give your answer to the nearest penny.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Take off the £500 allowance first, then find 40% of what is left.

byKey.all-taxed: You taxed all £828. The first £500 is tax-free, so only £328 is taxed.
byKey.allowance-taxed: That is 40% of the £500 allowance, which is the part that is not taxed.
byKey.kept: That is 60% of £328, the part the saver keeps. The tax is 40% of it: £131.20.

parts.question: Using tax of £131.20, what percentage of the £18,000 does the saver keep as interest after tax? Give your answer as a percentage to 2 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Take the tax from the interest, then divide by the £18,000.

byKey.gross: That is the rate before tax. The saver keeps $828 - 131.20 = 696.80$, which is 3.87%.
byKey.all-taxed: That is 60% of 4.6%, as if all the interest were taxed. The £500 allowance is free, so it is 3.87%.
byKey.tax-share: That is the tax as a share of the £18,000. The saver keeps the rest of the interest: 3.87%.

explain.text: After tax the saver keeps $828 - 131.20 = 696.80$ pounds. As a share of the savings that is $696.80 \div 18{,}000 \approx 0.0387$, or 3.87%.

parts.question: A tax-free account pays 3.9% a year. Using the after-tax rate of 3.87%, which account leaves this saver more interest?

options.why: You compared the rates before tax. After tax the 4.6% account keeps only 3.87%.
You rounded 3.87% up to 3.9%. They differ by 0.03 percentage points, about £5.20.

feedback.correct: Correct. 3.9% of £18,000 is £702, which beats the £696.80 kept from the taxed account.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Compare what each account leaves after tax.

explain.text: The taxed account keeps 3.87% of the savings, £696.80. The tax-free account keeps all 3.9%, which is £702. So the lower headline rate pays more.
